reviews.review:
Warhammer 40 000 Space Marine is a nice 3rd person close combat and shooting game. Unfortunately, that is exactly what it is, nice. In short, it lacks depth. After about 3 hours, the game starts to repeat itself badly. You use the identical (very simple) melee combo against everything, use the same ranged weapons in the same way against the few enemies you actually want to shoot and utilize the fact that your team members can't die. After 5 hours, I had to stop, because the game could no longer provide any challenge outside cramping me into tight areas and fill them with enemies, so I was no longer able to dodge their attacks (and no, the game doesn't have block or parry). The reason it took so long the get bored of the repetitive gameplay is the fact that stomping through greenskins as an ultramarine feels awesome.

Overall: 6,5
Must play for any 40k fan. Multiplayer is still going strong!

The most striking aspect of Space Marine is the flawless art direction. This game absolutely nails the Warhammer art style and it is glorious to behold. 

As a game, it's a solidly enjoyable 3rd person shooter, but lacks that special sauce that makes you want to come back for more. That said, it absolutely deserves to be played. 

For those like me who aren't deeply interested Warhammer, this game is a very compelling introduction to the world. The basic elements of Ultramarines, Orks, Chaos, the Inquisition and, most enjoyably for me, the proverbs and lore that underpins the military world of the universe are brought into the picture slowly through the single player campaign in way that does not overwhelm. The game frequently presents various proverbs from the scriptural canon of the space marines, which are both hilarious but compelling at the same time (e.g. "Better to die for the emperor than to live for yourself", or "If a job is worth doing, it's worth dying for"). 

The weaponary is excellent. There aren't too many to choose from, but each behaves so differently that none are redundant. Often in games (e.g. Borderlands) there are tonnes of weapons but many are barely distinguishable, making them a waste of space. Every weapon in this game is unique and fun to learn. 

The single player campaign is good fun although it isn't quite as enjoyable as you'd want it to be because it gets very repetitive. Still, in short bursts its a lark and a treat for the eyes and ears. Playing on hard is probably the way to go to stretch the game out as it is a little short otherwise. 

The cons are:
- too much ammo - making it more scarce would have added drama and challenge
- the melee combat mechanics are a bit too imprecise - you can't select and lock your targets, but only can button mash
- too few types of baddies
- the battles can get quite repetitive, leading you to play in short bursts only

Overall, it's amazing. Loved the voice acting and the heroic Titus is an excellent protagonist. They've set up a sequel at the end of the game. I'd be very interested to see it.
Simple yet fun enough game for fans of warhammer.
